AfterObtained.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the only gap in this rollup was N1 (the unconsumed Rng.Niche stream and the wrong draw pattern), and sts2_rl/relics/sere_talon.py:24-32 now does NextItem-and-Remove over `sorted(curse_pool_ids())` on `run.rng_set.niche`, matching SereTalon.cs:39-45. guards.what: N1: `Rng.Niche` is named in C# and never consumed, and the draw PATTERN differs (PROMPT.md bug class 16)
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the port now draws on the named stream. sts2_rl/relics/sere_talon.py:24-32 now reproduces SereTalon.cs:39-45 exactly -- `sorted(curse_pool_ids())` then `run.rng_set.niche.next_item(...)` with the picked id removed after each draw, which is NextItem-and-Remove rather than the old `rng.sample`; the legacy RL path keeps random_curses. WAS: the call went to the legacy shared random.Random, so the stream was never advanced and every later draw off it read at the wrong position.

guards.what: N2: the candidate pool -- `ModelDb.CardPool<CurseCardPool>().GetUnlockedCards(...)` filtered on `CanBeGeneratedByModifiers` and ordered `orderby c.Id` (SereTalon.cs:34-37)
guards.rationale: cards/pool.py's curse_pool_ids() applies exactly the CanBeGeneratedByModifiers filter over CURSE_POOL, and the ORDER matters because it is the index space NextItem draws from. EXECUTED (relic_probes_b14.py sere-talon): the generatable pool is 10 ids and `opts == sorted(opts)` is True, so the sim's declaration order already equals C#'s `orderby c.Id` -- which is the reason the sibling neows_bones can call `sorted(curse_pool_ids())` and get the same list. Checked rather than assumed because a wrong order would be invisible outside the conformance harness. The unlock-state argument is a waiver of its own (the sim assumes full unlocks; the executed `git grep UnlockState -- sts2_rl` hits are the driver's own flag and event gates, not a card-unlock system). Rule 7: cards/pool.py and relics/neows_bones.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N3: the counts -- DynamicVar("Curses", 2m) and DynamicVar("Wishes", 3m) (SereTalon.cs:26-27) read as IntValue (lines 39, 49)
guards.rationale: CURSES = 2 and WISHES = 3 (sere_talon.py:17-18) match, and there is no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file, so both are the pinned non-ascension values. Re-read against the C# rather than trusting the port's docstring, per PROMPT.md bug class 19 -- which is exactly how this batch's sand_castle G1 was found.

guards.what: N4: distinctness -- C# removes each picked curse from availableCurses (SereTalon.cs:42); the Wishes are three copies of the same card and are NOT distinct
guards.rationale: sere_talon.py:24 passes distinct=True for the curses (random_curses' documented Neow's-Bones/Sere-Talon mode) and line 26-27 loops make_card('wish') three times with no distinctness at all, matching SereTalon.cs:49-53's `RunState.CreateCard(ModelDb.Card<Wish>(), Owner)` per iteration. Executed output confirms three separate 'wish' cards in the deck. Rule 7: cards/pool.py is not hashed here.

guards.what: N5: `CardPileCmd.Add(card, PileType.Deck)` (SereTalon.cs:44, :52) vs run.add_card (sere_talon.py:25, :27), and the curse-then-Wish ORDER
guards.rationale: run.add_card runs modify_card_being_added_to_deck before the append and after_card_added_to_deck after it (run.py:341-354), which are the sim's two deck-add hooks -- the same bracket CardPileCmd.Add provides. The order is load-bearing and matches: C# adds both curses (lines 39-45) before any Wish (lines 48-53), and the sim does the same, so a relic that reacts to a deck add (Darkstone Periapt's +6 Max HP on a gained Curse) sees the curses first on both sides. Rule 7: run.py and relics/darkstone_periapt.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N6: `undo_after_obtained` is not implemented, and the pickup adds 5 cards to the run deck
guards.rationale: The consequence, for the record: a conformance-runner relic swap leaves two curses and three Wishes in the deck, which the (id, upgrade_level) deck comparison reports. Per PROMPT.md v6 binding item 3, the ABSENCE of undo_after_obtained is faithful at every site: the helper has no C# counterpart -- nothing in the game un-picks a relic -- so a sim lacking it is not diverging from the source, which is the only question this audit asks. Flagged for its operational consequence only, which is a tooling defect and not a fidelity gap. Rule 7: relics/base.py:143-150 and conformance/runner.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N7: the relic holds no state (PROMPT.md classes 10, 13); `CardCmd.PreviewCardPileAdd` and `Cmd.Wait(0.75f)` (SereTalon.cs:46-47, :54-55); ExtraHoverTips (line 30)
guards.rationale: No fields beyond the two key consts, so nothing to reset on either side -- read both files, with sweep-reset's 'hold no state' bucket as corroboration only. The rest: RelicModel.Flash() / FlashSfx / base.Status = RelicStatus.* / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / UpdateDisplay / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Title / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.PreviewCardPileAdd / CardPreviewStyle are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter, sfx and hover text, the localized name, and animation timing.
